messages:
IncidentBot: [PAGER] severity=sev1 customer=Obsidian private-vpc=vpce-obs-01 impact=ingress+egress NLB unhealthy targets, elevated 5xx for customer endpoints :rotating_light:

Jamie (oncall): on it, paging NetOps and SRE. Slack huddle in 2m if needed. @NetOps @Ken @Alex M.

Alex M.: ack. grabbing connection info and checking NLB target health. first glance: lots of TARGET_UNHEALTHY for target group tg-obs-01, healthcheck failing with 502 from backend.

Priya: Customer Eng reports Obsidian seeing 502/504s across all environments behind their private NLBs. They say this started ~10:05 UTC and affects production only.

NetOps: pulling NLB logs now. seeing healthcheck IPs from the load balancer but responses time out from targets' ENIs. Could be SG or route issue.

Alex M.: running `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg-obs-01` -> majority Unhealthy (TCP:connection-refused / timeout).

Ken: checking security groups for the obs-prod instances. `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-obs-app` returns inbound rules allowing 0.0.0.0/0 tcp:443 and internal 10.0.0.0/16 for application ports. healthchecks originate from NLB nodes (different AZ IPs). if there's a host-level firewall they might be blocking.

Priya: Customer Eng: "we didn't change SGs or host firewalls. We had a config push to app side around 09:50 but that was rolled back at 10:00. issue looks network-level from our side"

Jamie (oncall): action list: 1) confirm NLB healthcheck source IPs + connectivity to backend 2) verify host firewall/conntrack exhaustion 3) check DNS / recent route changes 4) temporarily allow NLB healthcheck CIDRs in SGs if needed 5) consider re-registering targets or draining and reattaching.

NetOps: NLB health check source IPs (per AZ): 172.31.45.2, 172.31.46.2, 172.31.47.2. trying `telnet 172.31.45.2 80` from obs-prod-host1 -> no route. traceroute shows next-hop in customer-tenant subnet but drops at their edge ENI.

Alex M.: also seeing an uptick in conntrack table usage on obs-prod-host1: `conntrack -S` shows ephemeral allocations near max (established ~620k / limit 655360). might be conntrack exhaustion causing new healthchecks to be dropped.

Ken: that would explain intermittent accept/refuse. can we confirm netfilter logs? `sudo dmesg | grep conntrack` on host shows repeated nf_conntrack: table full messages at 10:07.

Customer Eng (Obsidian): we have an outbound NAT change this morning for egress to proxy pool (10.200.0.0/16). Could that have shifted source IPs for healthchecks going to upstream services? We didn't touch host firewalls.

Priya: note: this is a private deployment. Redwood control plane changes shouldn't impact customer VPC routing, but customer NAT changes could expose new behavior.

Jamie (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) increase conntrack limit on affected hosts to buy time 2) temporarily add permissive SG rule to allow NLB healthcheck CIDRs -> NetOps to apply 3) re-register targets in tg-obs-01 4) set DNS TTL to low for any CNAMEs we might change (coordinate with Obsidian)

NetOps: applying SG change now: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-obs-app --protocol tcp --port 80 --cidr 172.31.0.0/16 --dry-run` -> then apply. updating.. :white_check_mark: added allow from NLB subnet ranges to port 80/443 on sg-obs-app.

Alex M.: bumping conntrack on hosts: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1310720` and persisting via /etc/sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf. applying on obs-prod-host1/2/3. monitoring.

IncidentBot: deploy-bot: rolling-restart request queued for target group tg-obs-01 by Alex M. Reason: re-register unhealthy targets.

Ken: after SG change and conntrack bump, healthchecks start returning OK for some targets. `describe-target-health` now shows 75% healthy. still seeing a handful of hosts flapping.

Customer Eng (Obsidian): We see traffic normalizing for a subset of endpoints. thank you. we may need a root cause investigation on our NAT change.

Priya: checking DNS: Obsidian uses private hosted zone obs.internal with ALIAS pointing to NLB. no recent Route53 changes. TTLs are 60s.

Jamie (oncall): secondary mitigation: shift a small percent of traffic to dedicated failover pool (dedicated-obs-backup) while we stabilize. Priya coordinate with Customer Eng to authorize cross-pool shift.

Customer Eng (Obsidian): authorize. move 15% traffic to dedicated-obs-backup for 30m.

NetOps: initiating partial traffic shift via weighted DNS / ALB target group weights. `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes` to adjust stickiness/weighting. executing...

Alex M.: monitoring latency and error rates. 15% shift stable, overall 5xx down from 18% -> 3% for the customer endpoints.

Ken: root cause hypothesis: Obsidian's NAT change increased ephemeral port reuse and caused conntrack saturation on a subset of hosts; combined with host-level firewall drop rules for unexpected source IPs meant NLB healthchecks timed out -> ELB marked targets unhealthy -> traffic funneled to remaining hosts -> cascading conntrack pressure.

Priya: next steps: 1) runbook item for customers doing NAT pool changes (notify Redwood/pair rollout) 2) ensure conntrack defaults for private deployments are higher / have automation to scale 3) formal post-incident review with Obsidian.

Jamie (oncall): timeline & summary for SRE pager: `10:05 UTC - Obsidian reported elevated 5xx; 10:07 - conntrack table full on multiple hosts; 10:12 - SG updated to allow NLB CIDRs; 10:16 - conntrack bumped; 10:25 - partial traffic shift to backup; 10:45 - majority targets healthy; 11:00 - incident declared mitigated, monitoring.`

IncidentBot: incident ticket INC-2026-3187659999 created, severity=sev1, assignee=Jamie (oncall), linked runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-nlb-healthcheck.

NetOps: leaving temporary SG rule in place for 1h as safety. will remove after stabilization window unless customer requests extension.

Customer Eng (Obsidian): thanks team — we'll revert NAT change in a controlled window and follow up with our network team. appreciate the quick help.

Jamie (oncall): handoff to follow-up rotation: @Ken taking root cause owner, @Priya coordinating customer postmortem. I'll add notes to the ticket and update status check-in at +4h. If any regressions, re-open channel. :thumbsup:
